newsitem.title: UK: P&U recovery plan meets analyst scepticism.
newsitem.headline: P&U recovery plan meets analyst scepticism.

text.p: Further gloom surrounded prospects for a turnaround at Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc, after analysts damned the group's recovery programme as thin and vague.
They also said there was little credible explanation of the company's poor first-quarter performance, when sales dropped by more than six percent and earnings per share fell by nearly 16 percent.

Daiwa analyst Nigel Keegan, who has an "out and out sell" on the stock after last week's profit warning, said: "I see nothing in the results which could explain just how bad they are, and nothing in the plans for the future that will change this situation. They seem to be trying to spend their way out of trouble, which is the last thing they should be doing."
Robert Uhl, analyst at Salomon Brothers in New York, said "It is just one disappointment after another," and added that there was nothing new or exciting in the recovery strategy.
